pattern_stance_changes.reason: P17 is static or linter feedback inside an agent loop. Phoenix is a standalone LLM bug-finder whose alarms go to human triage (§III-E, §IV-D), and no coding agent consumes its output. The only static comparison is against Bandit and the Clang Static Analyzer (Table II), and those conventional analyzers score 99-100% FP on this bug class. So the paper gives no evidence on in-loop static feedback, and if anything it shows generic linters are useless here.

missed_issues: P05 'supports' is kept, but its ablation (Table IV, w/o ERG) compares grounded retrieval with no code context at all. It shows that grounding cuts hallucinated bridges; it says nothing about lexical versus embedding or graph retrieval, which is the harness decision P05 informs.

The ablation counts are single runs. The 10 SBIR repeats per item (§IV-A) widen sampling rather than measure variance, so small deltas such as w/o summary 27 vs 31 bugs cannot be separated from LLM nondeterminism.

hype_language: the abstract says '31 real new bugs', but only 26 are maintainer-confirmed (Table III). The other 5 are 'real' on the first two authors' judgment, which makes the 13.89% FP rate a lower bound (10/36 = 27.8% if the unconfirmed are counted as false).

Fuzzer comparison (Fig. 7): there is no time or compute budget, no version window, and no statement on whether fuzzer-found bugs were triaged or confirmed by the same standard. The overlap analysis may therefore compare unequal efforts.
Total SBIRs generated (56 items × 10) and how they were deduplicated into 36 alarms are not reported, so the work behind each alarm is unknown.
Scope: this is DL-framework bug finding, not agentic coding-harness design, which limits its weight for harness decisions.
note: I agree with admit_with_caveats; the maintainer-confirmed, merged patches are real external evidence. However, P17 'supports' misreads a standalone LLM bug-finder as in-loop static feedback, and P05's ablation tests grounding against nothing rather than against another retrieval method.
